## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (no finding or checklist failure at or above the critical threshold; one important checklist failure and ten suggestions remain)

This PR is ready to merge: it meets all eight acceptance criteria, and nothing at the critical threshold blocks it, but one important classifier gap and several small doc and test notes are worth fixing.
Rule applied: rule 6 — a finding or checklist FAIL below the threshold, or an INCONCLUSIVE item, remains → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

prflow:code-reviewer returned no findings.

### 🟠 Important / Major

- VC-30: FAIL (important) — The docstring asserts introspection is a statement whose first keyword is SHOW, or a statement that references any catalog table, even alongside data tables. [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:112]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Table-reference half holds: readonly.py:140-147 uses parsed.find_all(exp.Table), which walks subqueries, EXISTS and CTE bodies; schema is lowercased (quoted mixed-case ok), backticks are handled by the mysql parser, and three-part names put information_schema in table.db. The SHOW half does not hold: line 131 uses first_sql_keyword (lines 38-49), which only strips whitespace and leading '(' and returns split()[0].upper(). For '/* c */ SHOW TABLES' or '-- c\nSHOW TABLES' it returns '/*' or '--', not 'SHOW'. The MySQL read-only guard explicitly accepts comments (_mysql_parse_sql, readonly.py:401-477), so such a statement is executable. It then falls through to sqlglot parsing, where exp.Show has no catalog Table node, so the function returns False. The docstring says 'a statement whose first keyword is SHOW' is introspection, but a SHOW with a leading comment is classified as a data query and its result is not withheld. The docstring's best-effort note (lines 127-129) exempts only unparseable non-SHOW queries, not this case.

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (10)

<details><summary>10 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 75-106: `_CATALOG_SCHEMAS_BY_DIALECT` and `_CATALOG_NAME_PREFIXES_BY_DIALECT` must have the same keys, and must match what `sqlglot_dialect_for_url` returns, but only a comment enforces this. `_catalog_names` checks membership in the schemas dict and then indexes the prefixes dict directly, so a key added to one dict only would raise `KeyError` outside the classifier's `try`. Today the key sets agree. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/tools/_format.py` lines 251-254: `dialect` is an open `str`. A name that sqlglot does not know may make `sqlglot.parse_one` fail, and the classifier then fails open to `False`, so catalog results would be shown. The production caller always passes `sqlglot_dialect_for_url(...)`, so no reachable input triggers this today. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/tools/_format.py` lines 565-576: `components_to_markdown` takes no `dialect` and calls `components_to_blocks(components)`, so it always classifies under the all-engine union, while the module docstring still calls it "the same walker". Nothing in `src/` calls it. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `src/sqllens/tools/_format.py` lines 386-394: a withheld introspection DataFrame is dropped without a log line. An operator cannot tell "the agent produced nothing" from "the formatter hid a result", while the same function logs similar decisions at INFO. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. `src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py` lines 133-136: the existing `except Exception: return False` now also decides whether a catalog result is shown, and it leaves no server-side record when a parse failure under the configured dialect lets a catalog result through. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. `docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md` line 55: the sentence "withholds from the user the result of every `run_sql` query the introspection classifier marks as introspection" is broader than the code. For a `SHOW` statement, `RunSqlTool` returns a row-count notification instead of a DataFrame, and that notification can still reach the Markdown on a turn with no blocks. (raised by 1/6 agents)
7. `docs/internal/database-connectors/read-only-safety.md` line 68: "`pg_catalog` for `postgres` and `mysql`, `sys`, `performance_schema` for `mysql`" can be read as "`pg_catalog` for postgres and mysql". The code scopes `pg_catalog` to `postgres` only. (raised by 1/6 agents)
8. `src/sqllens/tools/_format.py` lines 360-361: the new comment says "row counting above still sees it", but the row-count update the DataFrame feeds is below, at lines 398-400. (raised by 1/6 agents)
9. `tests/unit/test_format.py` lines 1954-1957: two "leave unchanged" items from acceptance criterion 7 have no test. No test covers a chart emitted after an introspection `run_sql` card. `test_unparseable_sql_result_still_shown` runs only with `dialect=None`, so fail-open under a configured dialect is not covered. (raised by 1/6 agents)
10. `docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md` lines 110-116 and line 193: the `sqllens/blocks` wire-contract bullets and the `query_database_impl_with_widgets` paragraph still describe table and one-row text blocks without the new introspection exception. Only the DATAFRAME rule row (line 102) was updated. (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred (3)

<details><summary>3 items</summary>

- VC-14: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The unchanged sentence stating that out of the box the run_sql tool-arguments STATUS_CARD never reaches the calling client still holds now that build_agent always admits DEFAULT_USER_GROUP to UI_FEATURE_SHOW_TOOL_ARGUMENTS. [docs/internal/agent/factory.md:132]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  docs/internal/agent/factory.md:132 says that out of the box the run_sql tool-arguments STATUS_CARD never reaches the calling client, and gives the framework default gate plus the static 'default' group as the reason. Reading the head text shows that reason no longer holds for build_agent. Line 134 of the same file says build_agent always admits DEFAULT_USER_GROUP, so the agent always emits the card into the component stream. src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:293-303 confirms it: components_to_blocks always sees the card, and only `if not effective.show_details: query_info = None` keeps the SQL from the MCP client. The agent trace is built only when show_details is on (lines 308-318). So at the MCP-client level the claim holds with default config, because the SQL and card are withheld, but by a different mechanism than the sentence states. At the component-stream level the sentence is now false. Whether it means 'client' as the MCP caller or as the stream consumer is ambiguous. I found no requirement text that is unchanged in both views and outside the subject files to make this a FAIL. The one candidate, base docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md:244, describes the old gating and was not shown to be unchanged in the head. INCONCLUSIVE. The sentence is stale or misleading wording at most: 'never reaches' is true only if 'client' means the MCP caller.

  </details>

- VC-28: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — For a schema-qualified table such as information_schema.columns, pg_catalog.pg_tables, mysql.user, sys.schema_table_statistics or performance_schema.threads, sqlglot's `exp.Table.db` returns the schema qualifier as a string under the mysql, postgres and sqlite dialects and under no dialect, so the lowercased value is compared against the catalog schema set. [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:140]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The code at src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:140-143 does use `(table.db or '').lower()` against the catalog schema set. The claim is about sqlglot's `exp.Table.db` behaviour, and the sqlglot source (sqlglot/expressions.py) is not in the supplied views. Globs for sqlglot/expressions* under the repo and common Python locations found nothing. I did not run sqlglot to parse the example queries under each dialect.

  </details>

- VC-29: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — `sqlglot.parse_one(sql, dialect='mysql')` parses `SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = DATABASE()` without raising, so the MySQL catalog query is classified as introspection rather than falling into the fail-open `except Exception: return False` branch. [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:133]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  readonly.py:133-138 does fail open to False on any parse exception, so the claim matters. I could not execute sqlglot (no run tool). Static trace of installed sqlglot (.venv/.../sqlglot/parser.py): dialects/mysql.py has no DATABASE handling; tokens.py:292 maps DATABASE to TokenType.DATABASE; that token is in ID_VAR_TOKENS (via CREATABLES/DB_CREATABLES, parser.py:710-740, 757-867) but NOT in FUNC_TOKENS (parser.py:923-974), and _parse_function_call (parser.py:7551-7562) returns None for a non-FUNC token followed by '('. That suggests DATABASE parses as a Column and the '(' is left over, which would raise a ParseError (fail-open), contradicting the claim. But the repo tests (tests/unit/test_safety.py:826-830) expect True for this exact SQL, and the tokenizer may be a compiled/other implementation I could not read, so I cannot settle it by reading. Missing evidence: running sqlglot.parse_one('SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = DATABASE()', dialect='mysql') in the project venv, or the pinned sqlglot version's tokenizer/test_mysql coverage.

  </details>

</details>

On a MySQL database, a catalog query such as `SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = DATABASE()` is classified as introspection and its result is not shown. checklist.claim: The docstring asserts introspection is a statement whose first keyword is SHOW, or a statement that references any catalog table, even alongside data tables.
checklist.source_excerpt:
Schema introspection = a statement whose first keyword is ``SHOW``, or a
    statement that references any catalog table, even alongside data tables.
checklist.verify_hint: Trace inputs that could falsify it: a catalog table referenced only inside a scalar subquery, EXISTS, or CTE body; a quoted mixed-case schema ("Information_Schema".tables) or MySQL backticks; a three-part name db.information_schema.columns; a SHOW preceded by a comment or parentheses
checklist.evidence: Table-reference half holds: readonly.py:140-147 uses parsed.find_all(exp.Table), which walks subqueries, EXISTS and CTE bodies; schema is lowercased (quoted mixed-case ok), backticks are handled by the mysql parser, and three-part names put information_schema in table.db. The SHOW half does not hold: line 131 uses first_sql_keyword (lines 38-49), which only strips whitespace and leading '(' and returns split()[0].upper(). For '/* c */ SHOW TABLES' or '-- c\nSHOW TABLES' it returns '/*' or '--', not 'SHOW'. The MySQL read-only guard explicitly accepts comments (_mysql_parse_sql, readonly.py:401-477), so such a statement is executable. It then falls through to sqlglot parsing, where exp.Show has no catalog Table node, so the function returns False. The docstring says 'a statement whose first keyword is SHOW' is introspection, but a SHOW with a leading comment is classified as a data query and its result is not withheld. The docstring's best-effort note (lines 127-129) exempts only unparseable non-SHOW queries, not this case.
